sessions.title: Interactive Counter Component
strengths: Could reason about the requirements before knowing the React syntax.
Identified that the parent should own the counter state.
struggles: Declarative React thinking versus imperative DOM manipulation.
learned: Components are JavaScript functions that return JSX.
State belongs inside the appropriate component.
Event handlers receive functions rather than immediately executing them.
Parent components can pass state to children through props.
Updating state causes React to re-render the relevant UI.
sessions.recurring_weakness: React fundamentals are currently much less familiar than general JavaScript reasoning.
sessions.recurring_strength: Can reason about program structure and data flow even when the framework syntax is unfamiliar.

sessions.title: Shopping Cart Item Quantity Adjuster
strengths: Recognized that productName and initial quantity should be received as props
Recognized that quantity modification requires state
Identified the intended responsibilities of ShoppingCartItem
Identified the broader reasoning problem after reviewing the failed attempt
Was able to independently diagnose the weakness in the problem-solving approach after the session
struggles: Relational reasoning between concepts, components, and their responsibilities
Thinking about the overall scope of the challenge before focusing on individual variables and implementation details
Connecting React concepts together into a coherent component and data-flow model
Understanding React component rendering versus ordinary function calls
learned: The primary difficulty was not understanding individual React concepts, but understanding how they relate to one another within the scope of a challenge
The overall problem should be understood before reasoning about individual variables or implementation details
Props, state, event handlers, and components need to be understood relationally rather than as isolated concepts
The session produced a useful meta-thinking insight about how to approach future coding challenges
reinforce: Reading the full problem and identifying its scope before implementation
Connecting React concepts into a complete component/data-flow model
Using pseudocode after understanding the relationships between the parts of a problem
sessions.recurring_weakness: Difficulty reasoning about how individual concepts and components relate to one another before implementation
sessions.recurring_strength: Able to identify individual concepts and responsibilities, then reflectively diagnose weaknesses in their own problem-solving approach
